implementation.improvement: Added monotonic saturating exponential retry backoff after known FULL/LOSS/EAGAIN pressure. Repeated flush attempts during an active retry window now return local EAGAIN without issuing another pressure query or batch ioctl.
implementation.bounds: Backoff defaults to 1 ms, doubles up to a 100 ms cap, and uses overflow-safe monotonic deadline arithmetic. The configuration setter rejects zero, inverted, and over-cap values.
implementation.recovery: Successful submission and explicit loss acknowledgement reset the retry window. Pressure state remains authoritative after the backoff expires.
implementation.security: The optimization only suppresses redundant userspace retries; it does not bypass the kernel ioctl, capability checks, lineage checks, tenant accounting, or telemetry-loss handling.

productivity_interpretation.benefit: Under known pressure, repeated flush attempts no longer consume a pressure query and kernel batch ioctl per retry. The unit test directly verifies one local fast rejection with unchanged query and flush counters.
productivity_interpretation.raw_throughput_scope: The integrated gate retained the inherited M155 synthetic QEMU accounting benchmark at speedup_x100=167 in this run; M159 does not claim an isolated raw-throughput gain because its measured benefit is retry-control overhead reduction.
productivity_interpretation.hardware_scope: No physical accelerator throughput, latency, or power claim is made.

build_artifact.kernel_source: M156 kernel image reused; M159 is userspace runtime/test integration.

release_gate.reason: M159 is bounded userspace/QEMU validation. Physical accelerator qualification, independent reproducible production builders, signed artifacts, stable/LTS forward-port qualification, and external security governance remain required.
release_gate.hardware_claim: No physical GPU, NPU, VRAM, IOMMU, DMA, vendor-driver, reset, or fleet qualification is claimed.

known_limitations: Backoff timing is a userspace optimization and does not replace kernel-side backpressure enforcement.
A monotonic clock failure disables the fast path for that call rather than guessing a deadline; correctness remains fail-closed through the normal pressure query.
The unit test deterministically validates counters and behavior; QEMU validates integration and packaging, not physical accelerator behavior.
No isolated M159 raw-throughput improvement is claimed; the M155 benchmark remains supporting context only.
The kernel remains based on the Linux v7.2-rc7 development line and production release qualification remains incomplete.
